name: Rigid-body knockdown
doc: Stacks of crates, planks and balls on a floor (a small Box2D-lite rigid-body world on the CPU: box and ball contacts, friction, warm-started impulses) that the kick knocks over: each bass-heavy onset throws the most intact structure up and apart, harder the louder it is, with a floor shock ring and a camera jolt; lighter onsets rattle what stands. Between hits the pieces float back to their slots as glowing see-through ghosts and stack up again from the bottom row.

palette.doc: stop 0 is the wall, the middle stops the bodies (each structure its own), the top stops flashes, rings and ghosts

impulse.doc: kick strength; loudness scales it further (0 = no kicks)

restack.doc: how firmly knocked pieces fly back to their slots (0 = they stay where they fall)

idle.doc: seconds without a kick before a soft kick of its own on quiet music (0 = never)

view.doc: world units across the screen height (the stage is 1.8 wide)

cycle.doc: palette drift of the bodies, sweeps per 16 beats
